strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Extends the Rust-owned aggregate progress overview with actionable headless route candidates derived from current runtime state.
Lets a headless caller decide the next explicit continuation route from one bounded task.list response.
Keeps route availability and handles under Rust runtime derivation instead of VSIX or caller policy.
Uses bounded task records and provenance/ledger-derived progress state without exposing raw ledger payloads or appending new events.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances progress_visualization with supporting headless_autonomous_development, runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and subtask_orchestration.
answers.new_capability: Existing task.list progress_overview exposes bounded headless_route_candidates with route kind, current progress handles, task/run/proposal/apply handles when applicable, next action, priority, and route fingerprint.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M10 progress overview exposes coarse task sets and next-action groups, but it predates M11-M33 explicit headless continuation routes and does not provide route handles for current continuation decisions.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Headless callers must continue scraping individual inspections or duplicating runtime route policy to choose recovery, retry, provider retry, or parent-join continuation actions.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M31-M33 added context-read, recovery-run, and parent-join execution routes; M34.1 makes current routes discoverable through progress visualization.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The implementation extends existing task.list progress_overview and adds no JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: No separate summary surface is added. The bounded candidate collection is part of the existing progress overview and is the capability itself, not a report/history/digest/readiness wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime now computes deterministic actionable route candidates from current task records and bounded provenance state during task.list.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can choose the next explicit runtime call from one bounded progress overview instead of implementing Brownie route policy outside Rust.
answers.milestone_progress: This is the first M34 vertical slice and aligns runtime progress visualization with the current headless continuation capability set.

review_value_gate.review_intent: M34.1 must be reviewed for Rust-owned deterministic route candidate derivation, bounded metadata, read-only task.list behavior, and behavior tests proving caller decision capability.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M34.1 changes product runtime/protocol and phase manifests; guard engine files are not expected.

exit_criteria: Candidates are derived by the Rust runtime from current task records and bounded provenance/progress state, not caller-supplied or VSIX-computed values.
Candidate entries include route kind, progress fingerprint, aggregate sequence, deterministic route fingerprint, next action, priority, and applicable task/run/proposal/apply/fingerprint handles.
Candidate ordering and route fingerprints are deterministic for the same bounded source state.
Consumed or stale parent join evidence does not produce an executable parent-join route candidate.
task.list remains read-only and appends no ledger event.
VSIX protocol validators accept valid candidate arrays and reject invalid route kinds, malformed fingerprints, raw fields, and arbitrary percentage fields.
No new RPC, report, digest, history, readiness, preview, capability, verdict, or inspection wrapper is added.
No workspace mutation, task execution, verifier execution, provider call, shell/git/network/service action, or authorization consumption occurs.

Candidate payloads do not include raw prompts, provider responses, file content, raw diffs, raw hunks, stdout, stderr, commands, environment values, secrets, absolute paths, canonical paths, raw child output, or raw ledger payloads.

tests: VSIX protocol task list progress overview validation
